overall_assessment: Section extraction for HiOF is accurate in all 16 courses, including both random controls. The h2 headings split cleanly. Kunnskap/Ferdigheter/Generell kompetanse groups are all kept in learning_outcomes, arbeidskrav always land in coursework_requirements, Praksis is in teaching_methods, and Sensorordning, 'Vilkår for ny/utsatt eksamen', Arbeidsomfang, Undervisningssemester and Evaluering are dropped, so the earlier audit's problems are fixed. Every pre-pass flag is a false alarm: the 'boilerplate' prerequisite 'Bestått praksisperioder i N. studieår' is a real progression requirement, and the leak flags are set off by topic lines ('Ferdigheter i samfunnsfag', 'Arbeidsformer i samfunnsfag', 'litteraturhistorisk oversikt'). The missing reading_list in 10 of 16 courses is intended: a check across all HiOF plans shows those Litteratur sections hold only the Leganto pointer, which is suppressed as a placeholder (443 plans, plus 1 'vil være klart' note). Two cosmetic problems remain: reading-list date-stamp variants that slip past the #248 regex, and inline grading-panel lines inside assessment.

findings.description: The reading_list row starts with an administrative update stamp, which is not a reference. Two of the six reading_list rows in the packet show it ('Litteraturlisten er sist oppdater .' and 'Litteraturliste sist oppdatert .'). The canonical form 'Litteraturlisten er sist oppdatert 7. januar 2019.' is already stripped correctly (e.g. hiof_LMUSAM10417-1_2019_spring_2), but variant wordings get through. Across all HiOF, 26 of 360 reading_list rows still start with such a stamp. Other variants seen there: 'Litteraturen er sist oppdatert …', 'Litteratur er sist oppdatert …', 'Litteratur sist oppdatert .', 'Litteraturliste sist oppdatert 31. mai 2019.'
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In .clean_sections() (R/extract_sections.R), the #248 regex '^\s*Litteratur(?:listen|lista) er sist oppdatert[^\n]*\s*' needs the word 'listen'/'lista', the word 'er' and the full word 'oppdatert'. It misses 'Litteraturliste' (no -n), 'Litteraturen', bare 'Litteratur', a missing 'er', and the truncated 'oppdater'.
findings.suggested_fix: In .clean_sections(), broaden the reading_list pattern to '^\s*Litteratur\w*(?:\s+er)?\s+sist\s+oppdater\w*[^\n]*\s*' (case-insensitive). It stays anchored at the start of the row, so references are not touched.

findings.evidence: Oppgaven vurderes av en ekstern og en intern sensor.
findings.description: In NOR104 2020-2024 (5 of 16 courses), the grading-panel arrangement is written as lines inside the Eksamen block ('Oppgaven vurderes av en ekstern og en intern sensor.', 'Intern sensur.'), so it stays in assessment. When the same information sits under its own 'Sensorordning' heading, as in NOR104 2025, SAM104/114 and KHV113, the pipeline drops it as exam logistics (.drop). The same course therefore carries sensor text in assessment in some years and not in others. The assessment design itself is complete and correct, so the impact is cosmetic.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Sensorordning → .drop in R/section_heading_map.R only works when the text has its own heading. .strip_section_noise() (R/extract_sections.R) has no line pattern for inline sensor statements, so they stay in assessment.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hiof entry to .section_noise in R/extract_sections.R that removes whole lines only: '(?m)^(?:Oppgaven vurderes av (?:en )?ekstern og (?:en )?intern sensor|Intern(?: og ekstern)? sensu?r|To interne sensorer)\.?[ \t]*$'. Because it matches whole lines, 'Karakterregel' lines and design sentences are kept.
